title: TyCHO scene
description: Structure of scene.tys, version 0.5. The rules that this schema cannot express are in tycho-scene.md.

format.description: The format is always the string "tycho-scene". (rule `scene`)

version.description: The version of the scene format is written as "major.minor", e.g. "0.5". (rule `version`)

requires.description: The features that the scene uses are listed here, so that a runtime that does not implement one rejects the scene. (rule `version`)

generator.description: The program that wrote the scene is named here, e.g. pytycho with its version.

title.description: The title of the page is plain text. (rule `plain-text`)

theme.description: The colors and the font of the page are given here.

frames.description: The frames of the scene are declared here by id, and together they form one tree. (rule `frame`)

bodies.description: The bodies, i.e. named points such as the primary and the secondary, are declared here by id. (rule `body`)

trajectory_sets.description: The trajectory sets of the scene are declared here by id. (rule `trajectory-set`)

inputs.description: The inputs, i.e. the values that the person at the page can change, are declared here by id. (rule `input`)

clock.description: The clock, i.e. the time of the animation shared by every panel, is described here. (rule `clock`)

panels.description: The panels that a page may show are declared here by id. (rule `panel`)

controls.description: The controls are the widgets on the page that set an input or drive the clock. (rule `control`)

readouts.description: The readouts are the texts on the page that show current values.

initial.description: The state at the start, with the panels shown and the values of the inputs, is given here. (rule `state`)

steps.description: The steps are the named times of the timeline at which a presentation stops. (rule `steps`)

id.description: The step is found by this identifier, which differs from the ids of the other steps. (rule `identifier`)

at.description: The time of the step is given in seconds of the timeline, within one loop. (rule `steps`)

label.description: The name of the step is plain text, and it may be left out.

overlays.description: The overlays are texts and legends drawn over the whole panel area rather than in one panel.

id.description: An identifier consists of ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dots, and hyphens, with at least one character. (rule `identifier`)

name.description: A name of a channel, a parameter, an attribute, or an array of the data container is a nonempty string.

color.description: A fixed color is written #rrggbb, with two hexadecimal digits each for red, green, and blue.

theme.description: The theme gives the colors and the font of the page.

background.description: The background color of the page is #000000 by default.

foreground.description: The foreground color is used for text, axes, and every line without a color of its own, and it is #d8d8d8 by default.

grid.description: The color of the lines of a grid layer is #262626 by default.

font.description: A CSS font family is used for every text of the page and of a video.

gutter.description: The color of the gutters between panels in a video is a blend of the foreground and the background by default.

attr.description: An attribute scalar has the value factor * attrs[attr] + offset, where attrs[attr] is the attribute of the trajectory set in context. (rule `context-number`)
The attribute is read by this name from the attrs of the trajectory set in context.

factor.description: The attribute is multiplied by this factor, which is 1 by default.

offset.description: This offset is added after the factor, and it is 0 by default.

channelRef.description: A channel scalar has the value of the channel at the sample in context, hence it changes along the trajectory. (rule `context-number`)

channel.description: The channel is read by this name from the trajectory set in context.

constantScalar.description: A constant scalar is a number or an attribute, and it does not change along a trajectory. (rule `context-number`)

scalar.description: A scalar is a number, an attribute, or a channel, and the field that holds it determines which forms are allowed. (rule `context-number`)

point.description: A point is given by three scalars, its coordinates x, y, and z.

frame.description: A frame is a coordinate system, defined against its parent by an origin, a rotation, and a scale. The root frame has none of them. (rule `transform`)

label.description: The name shown for the frame is plain text, and it does not affect any computation.

axes.description: The three axis labels, e.g. ["x", "y", "z"], are used as the titles of the axes.

unit.description: The unit label, e.g. "DU", is appended to the titles of the axes.

parent.description: The frame is defined against the frame with this id, and only the root frame lacks a parent. (rule `frame`)

origin.description: The origin of the frame is given in the coordinates of the parent, as three scalars or at a body. It is 0 by default. (rule `origin`)

anyOf.description: The origin is placed at the position of a body, in the parent frame and in the same context. (rule `body-origin-cycle`)

body.description: The origin is placed at the body with this id.

rotation.description: The axes of the frame are turned against those of the parent by an angle about one axis. Without a rotation, the axes are parallel. (rule `transform`)

axis.description: The rotation is made about this axis of the parent.

angle.description: The angle is given in radians, in the right-handed sense, so that a point fixed in the parent appears in the frame rotated by this angle. (rule `transform`)

scale.description: One parent unit is this many units of the frame. The scale is 1 by default, and it is never zero. (rule `origin`)

body.description: A body is a named point, e.g. a primary of the three-body problem, without a radius or a shape. (rule `body`)

label.description: The name shown for the body is plain text.

frame.description: The position of the body is given in the frame with this id. (rule `body`)

position.description: The position is given by three constant scalars in the frame of the body. (rule `body`)

color.description: The body is drawn in this color, and in the foreground of the theme by default.

image.description: A uint8 array of the data container with this name holds a PNG, JPEG, or WebP image, which is drawn in place of the disc of the body.

trajectorySet.description: A trajectory set holds trajectories that share a frame and a meaning, e.g. the members of a family of periodic orbits. (rule `trajectory-set`)

label.description: The name of the set is plain text. It is written by pytycho and not drawn by the runtime.

frame.description: The positions of the set are given in the frame with this id.

tags.description: The tags label the whole set, each a string value under a name, e.g. "family": "7". A set query finds sets by them. (rule `set-query`)

attrs.description: The attributes are numbers of the whole set, e.g. "mu": 0.01215. (rule `context-number`)

trajectories.description: The number of trajectories in the set is at least 1.

offsets.description: A uint32 array of shape (trajectories + 1,) with this name marks where each trajectory begins in the arrays of the set. Each trajectory has at least two samples. (rule `two-samples`)

positions.description: A float array of shape (S, 2) or (S, 3) with this name holds the position of every sample in the frame of the set, where S is the total number of samples. (rule `trajectory-set`)

channels.description: The channels are quantities stored at every sample, e.g. the time or the true anomaly, declared here by name. The name @index is reserved. (rule `index-channel`)

array.description: An array of shape (S,) with this name holds one value of the channel per sample.

interp.description: The value of the channel between samples is "linear", the default, or "hold", which keeps the value of the earlier sample. Only a channel part of a text reads it. (rule `timeline-parts`)

unit.description: The unit of the channel is plain text, e.g. "TU". It is written by pytycho and not drawn by the runtime.

parameters.description: The parameters are numbers stored once per trajectory, e.g. the Jacobi constant of each member, declared here by name. The name @index is reserved. (rule `index-channel`)

array.description: An array of shape (trajectories,) with this name holds one finite value of the parameter per trajectory.

label.description: The name shown for the parameter, e.g. in the title of a colorbar, is plain text. The name of the parameter is shown by default.

unit.description: The unit of the parameter is plain text, and it is appended to the title of a colorbar over the parameter.

periodic.description: With true, each trajectory is declared periodic, i.e. its last sample is the first sample again one period later. The default is false. (rule `periodic`)

input.description: An input is a value that the person at the page can change, of kind parameter, choice, or toggle. (rule `input`)

oneOf.description: An input of kind parameter holds a number, and the member whose value of the parameter is nearest to it is shown. (rule `members`)

parameter.description: The input holds a value of the parameter with this name, or the number of a member with the built-in parameter @index. (rule `index-channel`)

default.description: The value at the start is this finite number.

scope.description: With "shared", the default, the input has one value for the whole page, and with "per_panel" it has one value per shown panel. (rule `input-scope`)

oneOf.description: An input of kind choice holds one of a list of strings, e.g. the name of a frame or of a colormap.

values.description: The strings that the input may hold are listed here, each once.

labels.description: The text shown for each value is given here, one entry per value. The value itself is shown by default.

default.description: The value at the start is one of the values.

scope.description: With "shared", the default, the input has one value for the whole page, and with "per_panel" it has one value per shown panel. (rule `input-scope`)

oneOf.description: An input of kind toggle holds true or false, e.g. whether a layer is visible.

default.description: The value at the start is true or false.

scope.description: With "shared", the default, the input has one value for the whole page, and with "per_panel" it has one value per shown panel. (rule `input-scope`)

inputRef.description: A value is read from an input by its id. (rule `input-scope`)

input.description: The value is read from the input with this id. (rule `input`)

stringValue.description: A string is given as it is or read from an input of kind choice.

setQuery.description: A set query is the way a scene refers to a trajectory set, by its id or by its tags. (rule `set-query`)

oneOf.description: The set is referred to by its id.

set.description: The query matches the trajectory set with this id.

oneOf.description: The sets are found by their tags.

tags.description: The query matches every trajectory set whose tags contain all the given pairs. A value may be read from an input of kind choice.

memberRef.description: A member reference says which trajectories of a set are drawn: "all", one by index, an evenly spaced selection, or the one that an input of kind parameter selects. (rule `members`)

anyOf.description: One trajectory is selected by its number.

index.description: The trajectory with this number, counted from 0, is selected. A number at or past the count of trajectories is an error. (rule `members`)

anyOf.description: An evenly spaced selection of trajectories is made, which always holds the last one. (rule `members`)

evenly_spaced.description: About this many trajectories are selected, and every trajectory when it is at least the count. (rule `members`)

colormapName.description: A colormap is named after its matplotlib equivalent.

colormapByChoice.description: The colormap is picked by the panel's value of an input of kind choice.

input.description: The colormap is picked by the value of the input of kind choice with this id.

map.description: Every value of the choice, and only these values, is given a colormap name.

clock.description: The clock is the time of the animation, shared by every panel, so that all panels move together. (rule `clock`)

mode.description: In mode "fraction", every trajectory runs from its first to its last sample in one loop. In mode "epoch", every trajectory shows the same value of the clock channel. (rule `clock-mode`)

channels.description: The channels that may be the clock channel are listed here, and the person at the page switches among them with the playback control. (rule `monotone-clock-channel`)

labels.description: The text shown for each clock channel is given here, one entry per channel.

frame_count.description: The number of frame indices in one loop is an integer of at least 1. (rule `clock`)

range.description: In mode epoch, the clock channel runs through this range [a, b] of values over one loop. (rule `clock-mode`)

revolutions.description: In mode fraction, one loop covers this many revolutions of every periodic set. The default is 1. (rule `revolutions`)

seconds.description: The length of one loop is given in seconds at playback speed 1, and it is 8 seconds per revolution by default.

keyframes.description: In mode epoch, the shared value of the clock channel is given by keyframes over the timeline, in place of a range. (rule `clock-keyframes`)

end.description: With "loop", the default, the next loop starts at the end of a loop. With "stop", playback stops there. (rule `steps`)

colorSpec.description: A color is a fixed color, a colormap over a parameter or a channel, or a color by thresholds of a channel.

anyOf.description: Each trajectory takes one color from a colormap over a parameter.

parameter.description: The colormap is taken over the parameter with this name, which the set of the layer carries.

colormap.description: The colormap is a name or is picked by an input of kind choice.

range.description: This interval of values is mapped onto the colormap. It is the extent of the values over the set by default.

truncate.description: The part [a, b] of the colormap onto which the range is mapped lies within [0, 1], and it is [0, 1] by default.

anyOf.description: Each sample takes a color from a colormap over a channel, hence the color varies along the trajectory.

channel.description: The colormap is taken over the channel with this name, which the set of the layer carries.

colormap.description: The colormap is a name or is picked by an input of kind choice.

range.description: This interval of values is mapped onto the colormap. It is the extent of the values over the set by default.

truncate.description: The part [a, b] of the colormap onto which the range is mapped lies within [0, 1], and it is [0, 1] by default.

anyOf.description: Each sample takes the color c_j, where j counts the thresholds below the value of the channel.

channel.description: The thresholds apply to the channel with this name, which the set of the layer carries.

thresholds.description: The thresholds are given in increasing order.

colors.description: The colors are given one more than the thresholds.

trail.description: A trail of fixed length follows the moving point. (rule `trail-wrap`)

fraction.description: The length of the trail is a fraction of the whole loop, in (0, 1]. (rule `panel`)

taper.description: The width and the opacity fall linearly from the head to these fractions of themselves at the tail.

width.description: The width at the tail is this fraction of the width at the head, in [0, 1], and 0.25 by default.

opacity.description: The opacity at the tail is this fraction of the opacity at the head, in [0, 1], and 0.35 by default.

layer.description: A layer is one thing drawn in a panel, and its kind says what.

oneOf.description: In a trajectories layer, the selected members of a set are drawn as lines.

sets.description: The trajectories are taken from the set that this query resolves to. (rule `set-query`)

members.description: The members of the set that are drawn are selected here. (rule `members`)

reveal.description: With "none", the default, the whole trajectory is drawn. With "grow", it grows to the moving point, and with "trail", a trail follows the point. (rule `panel`)

trail.description: The trail is given here, and it is required when reveal is "trail".

head.description: With a head, the moving point is drawn as a marker. True gives the default marker, and false or an absent head gives none. (rule `head`)

anyOf.description: The marker of the head is written in the form of a marker and may also carry a glow.

color.description: The head is drawn in this color, and in the color of the layer at this point by default.

size.description: The width of the head is given in CSS pixels, or keyframed, and it is 9 by default.

shape.description: The shape is "disc", the default, "ring", "square", "diamond", "triangle", "star", "cross", or "plus".

edge.description: A filled shape is outlined in this color when it is given.

edge_width.description: The width of the outline, or of the stroke of a ring, a cross, or a plus, is given in CSS pixels. It is a sixth of the size by default.

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

glow.description: A disc is drawn behind the head while the channel of the member is positive, e.g. the plume of a thruster.

channel.description: The glow is shown while the channel with this name is positive, and the set carries it.

color.description: The glow is drawn in this color, and in #d62728 by default.

size.description: The diameter of the glow is given in CSS pixels, and it is 2.4 times the size of the head by default.

opacity.description: The opacity of the glow is in [0, 1], and it is 0.35 by default.

before.description: In mode epoch, "clamp", the default, holds a member at its first sample before it starts, and "hidden" hides it. (rule `before-after`)

after.description: In mode epoch, "clamp", the default, holds a member at its last sample after it ends, and "hidden" hides it. (rule `before-after`)

read_from.description: With "own", the default, each sample is transformed in its own context. With "reference", it is transformed in the context of the reference trajectory. (rule `read-from`)

fit.description: With false, the layer is drawn but left out of the camera fit. The default is true.

color.description: The color of the layer is the foreground of the theme by default.

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

width.description: The width of the line is given in CSS pixels, and it is 1 by default.

highlight.description: One member is drawn more prominently, the one that an input of kind parameter selects. (rule `members`)

input.description: The highlighted member is selected by the input of kind parameter with this id.

width.description: The width of the highlighted line is given in CSS pixels, and it is the width of the layer by default.

opacity.description: The opacity of the highlighted line is in [0, 1], and it is 1 by default.

kernel.description: The neighbors of the highlighted member are also brightened, with a Gaussian falloff in the parameter.

width.description: The width of the kernel is a fraction of the extent of the parameter over the set, in (0, 1].

opacity.description: The opacity at the center of the kernel is in [0, 1], and the opacity of the layer stays the floor.

visible.description: The layer is omitted while the toggle that this refers to is false. (rule `visible`)

clock.description: With a layer clock, the fractions along are computed by a channel of the layer's own. (rule `layer-clock`)

line.description: With false, only the heads are drawn, e.g. for a cloud of moving points. The default is true.

group_opacity.description: With true, each pixel that the lines cover is blended once at the opacity of the layer, so that overlaps do not build up. The default is false.

dash.description: The line is dashed with dashes of on and gaps of off CSS pixels, given as [on, off].

fill.description: Under a 2d camera, the area between the line and a base line is shaded where the line lies above the base.

base.description: The base line lies at this value of the second axis of the plane, and at 0 by default.

color.description: The fill is drawn in this color, and by default in the color of the layer when that is fixed, or in the foreground of the theme otherwise.

opacity.description: The opacity of the fill is in [0, 1], and it is 0.25 by default.

oneOf.description: In an arrow layer, a vector stored along each member is drawn as an arrow from the moving point. (rule `arrow`)

sets.description: The trajectories are taken from the set that this query resolves to. (rule `set-query`)

members.description: The members of the set that are drawn are selected here. (rule `members`)

vector.description: The components of the vector are read from the two or three channels with these names, in the frame of the set. The channel @index is not allowed. (rule `arrow`)

scale.description: The arrow is the vector times this constant scalar, in units of the frame. The default is 1. (rule `arrow`)

before.description: In mode epoch, "clamp", the default, holds a member at its first sample before it starts, and "hidden" hides it. (rule `before-after`)

after.description: In mode epoch, "clamp", the default, holds a member at its last sample after it ends, and "hidden" hides it. (rule `before-after`)

color.description: The arrow is drawn in this color, and in the foreground of the theme by default.

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

width.description: The width of the shaft is given in CSS pixels, and it is 1 by default.

head.description: The arrowhead is a filled triangle at the tip, 0.8 times as wide as it is long.

size.description: The length of the arrowhead is given in CSS pixels, and it is 10 by default.

visible.description: The layer is omitted while the toggle that this refers to is false. (rule `visible`)

clock.description: With a layer clock, the fractions along are computed by a channel of the layer's own. (rule `layer-clock`)

oneOf.description: In an inset box layer, the outline of the rectangle that another panel shows is drawn. (rule `inset-box`)

panel.description: The rectangle is the one shown by the first shown panel of the declared panel with this id, which has a 2d camera. (rule `inset-box`)

color.description: The box is drawn in this color, and in the foreground of the theme by default.

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

width.description: The width of the line is given in CSS pixels, and it is 1 by default.

dash.description: The line is dashed with dashes of on and gaps of off CSS pixels, given as [on, off].

min_size.description: On the screen, the box is at least this many CSS pixels wide and tall, and 8 by default.

visible.description: The layer is omitted while the toggle that this refers to is false. (rule `visible`)

oneOf.description: In a body layer, a body is drawn at the fraction along the reference trajectory. (rule `body-layer`)

body.description: The body with this id is drawn.

trail.description: With a trail, the path of the body over the trail of the reference trajectory is drawn as well. (rule `body-layer`)

size.description: The diameter of the body, or the width of its image, is given in CSS pixels, and it is 8 by default.

visible.description: The layer is omitted while the toggle that this refers to is false. (rule `visible`)

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

oneOf.description: In an axes layer, the coordinate axes of the display frame are drawn.

span.description: With "full", both directions of each axis are drawn across the panel, with "positive" only the positive half-axes, and with "box" a box around the plot under a 2d camera. The default is "full" under a 2d camera and "positive" under a 3d camera.

visible.description: The layer is omitted while the toggle that this refers to is false. (rule `visible`)

ticks.description: The axes of the plane that carry tick numbers in a box, "x" and "y", are listed here. Both are listed by default.

size.description: The height of the tick numbers of a box is given in CSS pixels, and it is 12 by default.

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

titles.description: The two texts given here replace the titles of the axes of the frame, e.g. with a subscript.

oneOf.description: In a grid layer, a grid of lines is drawn in the grid color of the theme.

labels.description: With true, the lines are numbered under a 2d camera. The default is true under a 2d camera and false under a 3d camera.

visible.description: The layer is omitted while the toggle that this refers to is false. (rule `visible`)

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

oneOf.description: In a label layer, a text is written at an anchor, above every other layer of its panel. (rule `label`)

text.description: The text is a string or a list of parts, read in the panel of the layer. (rule `timeline-parts`)

at.description: The anchor is a point, a member, or a fixed place on the screen. (rule `label`)

offset.description: The text is drawn [dx, dy] CSS pixels from the anchor, with dy pointing down the screen. The default is [0, 0].

align.description: The text is aligned along the line at its "start", the default, its "center", or its "end".

baseline.description: The text is aligned vertically at the "top", "middle", or "bottom" of its box, or at the "alphabetic" baseline of its last line. The default is "middle".

size.description: The height of the text is given in CSS pixels, and it is 13 by default.

color.description: The text is drawn in this color, and in the foreground of the theme by default.

weight.description: The weight of the font is "normal", the default, or "bold".

linespacing.description: The spacing of lines is given as in matplotlib, and it is 1.2 by default.

box.description: The text is drawn on a rectangle with this fill and edge.

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

leader.description: With a leader, a line is drawn from the anchor toward the text. True gives the default line.

anyOf.description: The leader is drawn with this color and width.

color.description: The leader is drawn in this color, and in the color of the text by default.

width.description: The width of the leader is given in CSS pixels, and it is 1 by default.

clock.description: With a layer clock, the fractions along are computed by a channel of the layer's own. (rule `layer-clock`)

visible.description: The layer is omitted while the toggle that this refers to is false. (rule `visible`)

oneOf.description: In a points layer, the stored samples of the selected members are drawn as markers. (rule `points`)

sets.description: The trajectories are taken from the set that this query resolves to. (rule `set-query`)

members.description: The members of the set that are drawn are selected here. (rule `members`)

marker.description: The samples are drawn with this marker, 4 CSS pixels wide in the foreground of the theme by default.

reveal.description: With "none", the default, every sample is drawn. With "grow", the samples appear one after another as the clock passes them. (rule `points`)

before.description: In mode epoch, "clamp", the default, holds a member at its first sample before it starts, and "hidden" hides it. (rule `before-after`)

after.description: In mode epoch, "clamp", the default, holds a member at its last sample after it ends, and "hidden" hides it. (rule `before-after`)

clock.description: With a layer clock, the fractions along are computed by a channel of the layer's own. (rule `layer-clock`)

fit.description: With false, the layer is drawn but left out of the camera fit. The default is true.

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

visible.description: The layer is omitted while the toggle that this refers to is false. (rule `visible`)

camera.description: The camera is the way a panel shows its display frame, as a flat picture of one plane or as a three-dimensional picture.

oneOf.description: A 2d camera shows a flat picture of one coordinate plane.

plane.description: The picture shows the plane "xy", the default, "xz", or "yz". (rule `panel`)

aspect.description: With "equal", the default, one unit is as long across the panel as up it. With "free", the two axes are scaled separately.

keyframes.description: The window that the panel shows is given by camera keyframes over the timeline. (rule `camera-keyframes`)

at.description: The time of the keyframe is given in seconds of the timeline.

width.description: The extent of the window along the first axis of the plane is given in units of the display frame.

height.description: The extent of the window along the second axis is given only under "aspect": "free", and the aspect ratio of the panel gives it otherwise.

center.description: The center of the window is given by two coordinates along the axes of the plane.

follow.description: The center follows the mean of the moving points of these targets, plus the offset. (rule `camera-keyframes`)

layer.description: The target is a member of the trajectories layer at this index of the layers of the panel.

member.description: The target is the member with this number in the set of the layer.

offset.description: This offset is added to the center of a follow keyframe, and it is [0, 0] by default.

ease.description: The window travels to this keyframe from the one before by this ease, and linearly by default. (rule `ease`)

oneOf.description: A 3d camera shows a three-dimensional picture that the person at the page can turn.

projection.description: With "perspective", the default, far objects look smaller. With "orthographic", parallel lines stay parallel.

up.description: The axis of the display frame that points up the screen is "x", "y", or "z", the default.

stretch.description: Every position is multiplied by these three positive factors along x, y, and z, which are 1 by default.

auto_rotate.description: The camera is turned about its up axis by this many degrees over each loop, and by 0 by default.

reference.description: The reference trajectory is the one trajectory that a panel follows, at which the bodies and the readouts of the panel are placed and read.

sets.description: The reference trajectory is taken from the set that this query resolves to. (rule `set-query`)

member.description: The reference trajectory is selected by its number or by an input of kind parameter. (rule `members`)

anyOf.description: The trajectory is selected by its number.

index.description: The trajectory with this number, counted from 0, is selected.

panel.description: A declared panel is one picture that a page may show, with a display frame, a camera, a reference trajectory, and layers. (rule `panel`)

label.description: The name shown in the header of the panel is plain text, and the id of the panel by default.

frame.description: The display frame, in which everything is drawn, is given by a frame id or by an input whose values are frame ids.

camera.description: The camera is the way the panel shows the display frame.

reference.description: The reference trajectory of the panel is given here.

layers.description: The layers are drawn in the order of this list, and a label layer is drawn above the others.

opacity.description: Every shown panel of this declared panel is faded by this opacity, in [0, 1] or keyframed, and 1 by default.

margin.description: The camera does not draw into these fractions of the height or the width of the panel, e.g. to leave room for tick numbers.

top.description: The margin at the top is a fraction of the height of the panel, and 0 by default.

right.description: The margin at the right is a fraction of the width of the panel, and 0 by default.

bottom.description: The margin at the bottom is a fraction of the height of the panel, and 0 by default.

left.description: The margin at the left is a fraction of the width of the panel, and 0 by default.

control.description: A control is a widget on the page that sets an input or drives the clock. (rule `control`)

oneOf.description: A slider sets an input of kind parameter and stops at the values of the parameter in its domain.

input.description: The slider sets the input of kind parameter with this id.

label.description: The name shown beside the slider is plain text.

domain.description: The slider stops at the distinct values of the parameter over the sets that this query matches.

oneOf.description: A tabs control sets an input of kind choice, with one tab per value, and a toggle control sets an input of kind toggle with a checkbox.

input.description: The control sets the input with this id.

label.description: The name shown beside the control is plain text.

oneOf.description: A playback control plays and pauses the clock and switches the clock channel. A scene without one is static.

readout.description: A readout is a text that shows current values, read at the reference trajectory.

place.description: With "panel", the readout is shown in each shown panel, and with "caption" it is shown once below the panels.

parts.description: The text is joined from these parts, without a format string. (rule `timeline-parts`)

layout.description: A layout node holds one shown panel or splits its area into two parts.

oneOf.description: A leaf holds one shown panel.

id.description: The leaf holds the shown panel with this id.

oneOf.description: A split divides its area into two parts, side by side or one above the other.

dir.description: With "row", the parts are side by side, and with "col" one is above the other.

ratio.description: The first part takes this fraction of the area, in (0, 1).

a.description: The first part is given by this node.

b.description: The second part is given by this node.

keyframes.description: The ratio is given by keyframes over the timeline, with values in [0, 1], and a part whose share is 0 is not drawn.

state.description: A state is everything that the person at the page can change, i.e. the shown panels, the values of the inputs, and the clock channel. (rule `state`)

inputs.description: The values of the shared inputs are given by input id, and an input without a value takes its default. (rule `input-scope`)

clock.description: The clock channel of the state is given here.

channel.description: The clock channel is the one with this name, one of the channels of the clock. (rule `clock`)

panels.description: The shown panels are given by id, each with its declared panel and its values of the per-panel inputs.

panel.description: The shown panel shows the declared panel with this id.

inputs.description: The values of the per-panel inputs in this shown panel are given by input id. (rule `input-scope`)

layout.description: The shown panels are arranged by this tree of layout nodes, which holds each of them once.

ease.description: An ease is the way a value travels to a keyframe from the one before: "linear", "smooth", "in", "out", "in-out", or "hold". (rule `ease`)

keyframes.description: A list of keyframes is written [t, v] or [t, v, ease] each, with the time t in seconds of the timeline. The times are nondecreasing. (rule `keyframes`)

keyframed.description: A keyframed value is the value that its keyframes give at each time of the timeline. (rule `keyframes`)

keyframes.description: The value is given by these keyframes. (rule `keyframes`)

opacity.description: An opacity is a number in [0, 1] or a keyframed value whose values lie in [0, 1]. (rule `timeline`)

size.description: A size is a positive number of CSS pixels or a keyframed value whose values are positive. (rule `timeline`)

layerClock.description: With a layer clock, a layer computes its fractions along in mode epoch by a channel of its own, through a range or keyframes. (rule `layer-clock`)

channel.description: The fractions along are computed by the channel with this name.

range.description: The channel runs through this range [a, b] of values over one loop. (rule `clock-mode`)

keyframes.description: The shared value of the channel is given by keyframes over the timeline. (rule `clock-keyframes`)

marker.description: A marker is a shape drawn at a point, as matplotlib draws a marker.

shape.description: The shape is "disc", the default, "ring", "square", "diamond", "triangle", "star", "cross", or "plus".

size.description: The width of the shape is given in CSS pixels, or keyframed. It is 9 for a head and 4 for a points layer by default.

color.description: A filled shape is filled with this color, and a ring, a cross, or a plus is stroked with it. It is the color of the layer for a head, and the foreground of the theme for a points layer, by default.

edge.description: A filled shape is outlined in this color when it is given.

edge_width.description: The width of the outline, or of the stroke of a ring, a cross, or a plus, is given in CSS pixels, or keyframed. It is a sixth of the size by default.

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

box.description: A box is a rectangle drawn behind a text.

fill.description: The box is filled with this color, and it is not filled by default.

edge.description: The box is outlined in this color, and it is not outlined by default.

edge_width.description: The width of the outline is given in CSS pixels, and it is 1 by default.

pad.description: The box surrounds the text by this many CSS pixels, and by 4 by default.

radius.description: The radius of the corners is given in CSS pixels, and it is 0 by default.

opacity.description: The opacity of the box is in [0, 1], and it is 1 by default.

textPart.description: A part of a text is a string, shown as it is, or a value, a subscript, or a superscript. (rule `timeline-parts`)

anyOf.description: The part shows the value of an input, a choice by its label and a toggle as on or off.

input.description: The value of the input with this id is shown.

digits.description: The number is shown to this many significant digits, from 1 to 17. Without it, an integer is shown as it is and any other number to six significant digits.

decimals.description: The number is shown with this many digits after the decimal point, from 0 to 17, in place of digits.

grouping.description: With true, the thousands of the integer part are separated by commas. The default is false.

factor.description: The number is multiplied by this factor before it is shown, and 1 by default.

offset.description: This offset is added after the factor, and it is 0 by default.

width.description: The number is padded with spaces on the left to this many characters, and 0 by default.

anyOf.description: The part shows the value of a parameter of the reference trajectory.

parameter.description: The value of the parameter with this name is shown, and the name @index is accepted.

digits.description: The number is shown to this many significant digits, from 1 to 17. Without it, an integer is shown as it is and any other number to six significant digits.

decimals.description: The number is shown with this many digits after the decimal point, from 0 to 17, in place of digits.

grouping.description: With true, the thousands of the integer part are separated by commas. The default is false.

factor.description: The number is multiplied by this factor before it is shown, and 1 by default.

offset.description: This offset is added after the factor, and it is 0 by default.

width.description: The number is padded with spaces on the left to this many characters, and 0 by default.

anyOf.description: The part shows the value of an attribute of the set of the reference trajectory.

attr.description: The value of the attribute with this name is shown.

digits.description: The number is shown to this many significant digits, from 1 to 17. Without it, an integer is shown as it is and any other number to six significant digits.

decimals.description: The number is shown with this many digits after the decimal point, from 0 to 17, in place of digits.

grouping.description: With true, the thousands of the integer part are separated by commas. The default is false.

factor.description: The number is multiplied by this factor before it is shown, and 1 by default.

offset.description: This offset is added after the factor, and it is 0 by default.

width.description: The number is padded with spaces on the left to this many characters, and 0 by default.

anyOf.description: The part shows the value of a channel at the fraction along the reference trajectory.

channel.description: The value of the channel with this name is shown. The channel @index is not allowed. (rule `index-channel`)

digits.description: The number is shown to this many significant digits, from 1 to 17. Without it, an integer is shown as it is and any other number to six significant digits.

decimals.description: The number is shown with this many digits after the decimal point, from 0 to 17, in place of digits.

grouping.description: With true, the thousands of the integer part are separated by commas. The default is false.

factor.description: The number is multiplied by this factor before it is shown, and 1 by default.

offset.description: This offset is added after the factor, and it is 0 by default.

width.description: The number is padded with spaces on the left to this many characters, and 0 by default.

anyOf.description: The part shows a value of the clock.

clock.description: The value is the "frame_index", the "frame_count", the shared "value" of the clock channel, or the "time" of the timeline in seconds. (rule `timeline-parts`)

digits.description: The number is shown to this many significant digits, from 1 to 17. Without it, an integer is shown as it is and any other number to six significant digits.

decimals.description: The number is shown with this many digits after the decimal point, from 0 to 17, in place of digits.

grouping.description: With true, the thousands of the integer part are separated by commas. The default is false.

factor.description: The number is multiplied by this factor before it is shown, and 1 by default.

offset.description: This offset is added after the factor, and it is 0 by default.

width.description: The number is padded with spaces on the left to this many characters, and 0 by default.

anyOf.description: The part shows the value of keyframes at the time of the timeline, e.g. a counter. (rule `keyframes`)

keyframes.description: The value shown is given by these keyframes.

digits.description: The number is shown to this many significant digits, from 1 to 17. Without it, an integer is shown as it is and any other number to six significant digits.

decimals.description: The number is shown with this many digits after the decimal point, from 0 to 17, in place of digits.

grouping.description: With true, the thousands of the integer part are separated by commas. The default is false.

factor.description: The number is multiplied by this factor before it is shown, and 1 by default.

offset.description: This offset is added after the factor, and it is 0 by default.

width.description: The number is padded with spaces on the left to this many characters, and 0 by default.

anyOf.description: The part shows the text of the last pair whose time has been reached, and the empty string before the first.

timed_text.description: The pairs [t, text] are given with nondecreasing times t in seconds of the timeline.

anyOf.description: The part is set as a subscript.

sub.description: This text is set as a subscript at 0.7 times the size, and as plain text in a readout.

anyOf.description: The part is set as a superscript.

sup.description: This text is set as a superscript at 0.7 times the size, and as plain text in a readout.

text.description: A text is a string or a list of parts. A newline character starts a new line. (rule `plain-text`)

anchor.description: An anchor is the place at which a label is written. (rule `label`)

oneOf.description: The anchor is a point, in the display frame or in another frame.

point.description: The point is given by three coordinates.

frame.description: The point is given in the frame with this id, and in the display frame by default.

oneOf.description: The anchor is the moving point of a member, with the fraction along clamped to [0, 1].

sets.description: The member is taken from the set that this query resolves to. (rule `set-query`)

member.description: The member with this number is followed.

oneOf.description: The anchor is a fixed place in the panel, inside its margin.

screen.description: The place is given as [fx, fy], the fractions of the width from the left and of the height from the top.

overlay.description: An overlay is a text or a legend drawn over the whole panel area.

oneOf.description: A text overlay is placed at a fraction of the panel area.

text.description: The text is a string or a list of parts. (rule `timeline-parts`)

at.description: The text is placed at [fx, fy], the fractions of the width and the height of the panel area.

align.description: The text is aligned along the line at its "start", the default, its "center", or its "end".

baseline.description: The text is aligned vertically at the "top", "middle", or "bottom" of its box, or at the "alphabetic" baseline of its last line. The default is "middle".

size.description: The height of the text is given in CSS pixels, and it is 13 by default.

color.description: The text is drawn in this color, and in the foreground of the theme by default.

weight.description: The weight of the font is "normal", the default, or "bold".

linespacing.description: The spacing of lines is given as in matplotlib, and it is 1.2 by default.

box.description: The text is drawn on a rectangle with this fill and edge.

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

oneOf.description: A legend overlay lists entries of a line, a marker, or colors with a label, laid out as matplotlib lays out a legend.

at.description: The legend is placed at [fx, fy], the fractions of the width and the height of the panel area.

entries.description: The entries fill the columns from the top down.

label.description: The label is a string, or a list of strings and subscript and superscript parts.

anyOf.description: The part is set as a subscript.

sub.description: This text is set as a subscript.

anyOf.description: The part is set as a superscript.

sup.description: This text is set as a superscript.

line.description: The entry is drawn as a short line.

color.description: The line is drawn in this color.

width.description: The width of the line is given in CSS pixels, and it is 2 by default.

dash.description: The line is dashed with dashes of on and gaps of off CSS pixels, given as [on, off].

opacity.description: The opacity of the line is in [0, 1], and it is 1 by default.

marker.description: The entry is drawn as this marker.

colors.description: The entry is drawn as short lines side by side in these colors, e.g. one per member of a family.

columns.description: The number of entries per row is all of them by default.

size.description: The height of the text is given in CSS pixels, and it is 13 by default.

color.description: The text is drawn in this color, and in the foreground of the theme by default.

align.description: The legend is aligned at its "start", "center", the default, or "end".

baseline.description: The legend is aligned vertically at its "top", the default, "middle", or "bottom", or at the "alphabetic" baseline.

opacity.description: The opacity is in [0, 1], or keyframed, and 1 by default.

handle_length.description: The length of the line of an entry is given in units of the size, and it is 2 by default.

handle_pad.description: The gap between the line and the label is given in units of the size, and it is 0.8 by default.

column_spacing.description: The gap between columns is given in units of the size, and it is 2 by default.
